This panoramic tour introduces you to the main attractions of one of South America's most European and cosmopolitan cities.
Travel along the famous 9 de Julio Avenue, home to two symbols of Buenos Aires: the magnificent Teatro Colón and the celebrated Obelisk.
Visit Plaza de Mayo, surrounded by some of the city's most important historic buildings, including Casa Rosada, the Metropolitan Cathedral and City Hall.
The itinerary also includes Plaza San Martín, Plaza Alvear and Congress Square.
Your route follows historic Avenida de Mayo and lively Corrientes Avenue.
Discover La Boca and San Telmo, colorful neighborhoods steeped in history, as well as the elegant districts of Palermo and Recoleta and modern Puerto Madero, a popular center for dining and entertainment.
Return to the hotel.
Overnight in Buenos Aires.

Over three hours, discover the historic and modern neighborhoods of Buenos Aires. Your Russian-speaking guide will show you La Boca and San Telmo, where Plaza Dorrego and its antiques market sit among bars and restaurants.

At Plaza de Mayo, you will see the presidential palace, Casa Rosada, associated with the history of Eva Perón. The route continues to the Obelisk on 9 de Julio Avenue. In Recoleta, discover the famous cemetery, the Basilica of Our Lady of Pilar and nearby cultural and shopping districts.

The tour also includes modern Puerto Madero, Lezama Park and Tres de Febrero Park. Along the way, see how the city changes from old houses and squares to broad avenues, green parks and waterfront developments.

This group excursion is included in the trip price. The evening tango show with dinner is offered as a separate part of the itinerary.

## City sightseeing tour with a Russian-speaking guide

The landmark obelisk is an emblem of Buenos Aires! La Boca keeps the spirit of the city's history alive! San Telmo is full of cafés and small restaurants. Plaza Dorrego is a favorite for antique lovers!

Buenos Aires is a city of wide boulevards, lush greenery and grand Art Deco buildings. It is a city where the pastel shades of old facades contrast with the bright colors of street artists. It is a city where tango is danced beneath a starry sky on a rooftop overlooking the river, while the aroma of grilled meat drifts through the air.

## History, art and landmarks

Buenos Aires is a city where you can lose yourself in a maze of narrow streets, find a cozy café-bar with live music and feel part of something special.

Discover a capital unlike any other and experience Argentina's legendary culture, with its rich blend of history and art. Buenos Aires is home to many of Argentina's most important attractions. The refinement of its architecture rivals Paris, yet the city has a beauty all its own. Buenos Aires is widely known for its museums, and art enthusiasts will find a great variety of museums, galleries, theaters and architectural landmarks here.

Among the city's principal attractions are the old district of La Boca and the historic San Telmo neighborhood, with its many large and small bars and restaurants and a genuine antiques market on Plaza Dorrego.

At the heart of Buenos Aires lies the central Plaza de Mayo. Other landmarks include the Pink House, the presidential palace of Casa Rosada, associated with Eva Perón, as well as many other monumental sights.

One of them is the city's symbol: a 67-meter obelisk standing on 9 de Julio Avenue, described as the widest street in the world, erected to commemorate Argentina's declaration of independence.

You will also visit the elegant Recoleta district, with its famous cemetery, the colonial-style El Pilar church and nearby cultural and shopping center.

The program also includes the city's modern areas: Puerto Madero, Lezama Park and Tres de Febrero Park.
